title: Phra Pathom Chedi, Nakhon Pathom
summary: Phra Pathom Chedi in Nakhon Pathom is a large bell-shaped chedi in the Sri Lankan style, about 120.5 m high. From 1853 King Mongkut (Rama IV) had a vast new chedi raised over an older chedi that had been left abandoned in the forest. He died before it was finished, and it was completed in the next reign.

uncertainty.note: Start is the year Rama IV began the great restoration that enclosed the older chedis, B.E. 2396 (Thai provincial PR office; Ramkhamhaeng University library). The sources opened do not give the completion year, only that it came in the reign of Chulalongkorn. The older Dvaravati-period chedi beneath is earlier but undated here. End is the present.

phases.description: Rama IV ordered a vast new chedi built over the older one in B.E. 2396 (1853) but died before it was finished (Ramkhamhaeng University library); the Fine Arts Department dates his reign to 1851-1868.
The work was completed in the reign of Chulalongkorn (Ramkhamhaeng University library); the sources opened give no completion year, so this phase starts where Rama IV's reign ended.

materials.material: brick masonry with lime plaster and a tile facing, over a structure of logs bound with chains (as described for the chedi in general)

reviewer_note: Shape stupa. Sources are in Thai and were read directly. The model describes the enclosing chedi, not the earlier ones. Height is 'about 120.5 m' in the Ramkhamhaeng page; search summaries give 120.45 m (not verified on a page I opened). The plan dimension is a circumference (about 233 m) because no diameter appears in the sources opened; the 1868 phase boundary is Rama IV's reign end, not a sourced completion date. A 'tallest stupa' claim is left out because no opened page supports it. The prd page also repeats the tradition that the first chedi was built in Ashoka's time, which is not used. Least sure of the completion date.
